findings.kind: raw ASCII mathematical formula in definition body
findings.repair: Put the group and generalized Fitting subgroup notation in math delimiters, e.g. $F^*(G)=F(G)E(G)$.

findings.kind: raw ASCII mathematical formulas in item body
findings.source_text: The nilpotent Hirsch length and growth degree need not agree: for the integer Heisenberg group H, h(H)=3 and D(H)=4; for $\operatorname{UT}_4(\mathbb Z)$, h=6 and D=10.
findings.rendered: H, h(H)=3 and D(H)=4 are plain text; h=6 and D=10 also plain text.
findings.repair: Typeset H and the invariant values consistently as math.

findings.kind: raw caret notation in item title
findings.source_text: title: "The Cartan matrix is D^T D"
findings.rendered: The Cartan matrix is D^T D; the caret is shown literally in the title.
findings.repair: Use math delimiters around $D^{\mathsf T}D$ in the title.

findings.kind: raw caret notation in item title
findings.rendered: Nonabelian extension obstruction in H^3; the caret is shown literally in the title.

findings.kind: raw underscore notation in item title

findings.rendered: S_3 and A_3 appear with literal underscores in the title.

findings.kind: raw subscript notation in item title

findings.rendered: Zp appears without a subscript in the title.
findings.repair: Use math delimiters around $\mathbb Z_p$ in the title.

existing_math_diagrams_checked.checks: The two exact rows run 1→N_i→E_i→Q_i→1; vertical maps α:N1→N2, β:E1→E2, γ:Q1→Q2 point downward. The square compatibilities are the standard ones i2∘α=β∘i1 and π2∘β=γ∘π1. Rendered arrows and labels agree; no reversal or index swap.

optional_candidates.candidate: Draw a short segment of the bi-infinite line with vertices n∈Z and translation arrows n↦n+3, then the quotient with orbit vertices [0],[1],[2] and edge orbits [0]—[1]—[2]—[0]. Verify the three distinct edge orbits and the closed 3-cycle, which directly witnesses the non-tree quotient.
optional_candidates.status: optional, source-supported; the prose already states the orbit classes and cycle, so the diagram is useful but not required.
